articles.summary: Quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) in the X-ray emission of accreting black hole binaries are commonly attributed to the relativistic Lense--Thirring precession of the inner accretion flow, in which a hot inner flow, tilted with respect to the black hole spin axis, precesses as a solid body while a cooler outer disc remains at its own, different tilt -- a warped, Bardeen--Petterson-type geometry. articles.title: Deep X-ray Observations of the Gamma-ray Bright Pulsar Wind Nebula HESS J1303-631
articles.summary: HESS J1303$-$631 is an evolved, TeV-bright pulsar wind nebula (PWN) powered by the energetic radio pulsar PSR~J1301$-$6305, offset by $\approx7'$ northwest of the TeV centroid, with an energy-dependent gamma-ray morphology. We present new, deep joint Chandra (108 ks) and XMM-Newton (102 ks) observations of this field. High-resolution Chandra ACIS imaging resolves the pulsar from a neighboring point source that XMM-Newton cannot separate. The pulsar's 2-10 keV spectrum is well described by an absorbed power law with $Γ=2.02\pm1.04$ and an unabsorbed luminosity of $3.44\times10^{31}\,{\rm erg\,s^{-1}}$ at $d=4.7$ kpc. articles.title: Detection Forecasting for Blazars at MeV Energies with Fermi-LAT Swift-BAT Cross Match
articles.summary: Over the past two decades, the lack of an MeV $γ$-ray all-sky instrument has left an observational gap in blazar broadband emission. Recently, a new suite of MeV $γ$-ray instruments with sensitivity in the $10^{-11}$ to $10^{-12}$ $\mathrm{erg/cm^{2}/s}$ range has been proposed, with the potential to far surpass the capabilities of previous all-sky MeV instruments. In this work, we forecast the capabilities of future MeV $γ$-ray instruments including COSI, GRAMS, newASTROGAM, and AMEGO-X to observe blazars. articles.title: Dark Matter Interpretations of the Galactic Center Gamma-Ray Excess with 18 Years of Fermi-LAT Data and the FL16Y Source Catalog
articles.summary: We investigate dark matter (DM) interpretations of the Galactic Center Excess (GCE) using 17.7 years of Fermi-LAT data and the FL16Y source catalog. We test 80 Galactic diffuse-emission models and include correlated systematic uncertainties from Galactic-plane control regions. We derive combined 95\% CL annihilation limits from 30 dwarf spheroidal galaxies (dSphs), including $J$-factor uncertainties, and compare the GCE-preferred regions with these limits and AMS-02 antiproton bounds. articles.title: The EMA Justitia Probe: Terminator Frame-Based Deployment Orbit Selection and Surface Coverage Analysis
articles.summary: The Emirates Mission to the Asteroid Belt (EMA) probe is designed to perform asteroid imaging during an uncontrolled ballistic descent to (269) Justitia. The mission design is constrained by main spacecraft proximity operations, uncertain asteroid gravity, limited knowledge of the final deployment trajectory, and requirements for illumination and safe operations. articles.title: The accretion flow and jet of M87: broadband modelling across spatial scales
articles.summary: The nearby radio galaxy M87 is an ideal laboratory for studying accretion flows and relativistic jet emission. The EHT collaboration conducted the most comprehensive multi-wavelength observational campaign of M87, in which radio instruments with resolutions ranging from tens of microarcseconds to about an arcsecond sampled different portions of the outflow. We model these data using a radiatively inefficient accretion flow (RIAF) with winds and a new multi-zone jet model, initially magnetically dominated, in which we solve the transport equation for the non-thermal electrons as they are injected, advected, and cooled along the jet. articles.title: Disc breaking and parametric instability in warped accretion discs driven by differential precession
articles.summary: We present the first local simulations of accretion disc breaking (or disc tearing) with differential precession. Precession can occur due to a non-spherical potential (e.g. tilted circumbinary discs), or relativistic effects (e.g. tilted discs around spinning black holes). articles.title: Competitive roles of turbulence and magnetic field on the formation of unipolar outflows in isolated molecular cloud cores
articles.summary: We investigate the impact of turbulence and magnetic field on the formation of unipolar outflows in the gravitational collapse of isolated low-mass cloud cores using three-dimensional non-ideal magnetohydrodynamics simulations. In the models explored in this study, we find that unipolar outflows are formed in cloud cores with the super-Alfvénic turbulence of $M_{\rm{A}}>1$, where $M_{\rm{A}}$ is the Alfvén Mach number of the initial cloud core. In contrast, bipolar outflows are formed in cloud cores with $M_{\rm{A}}\lesssim1$. articles.title: Probing the Interstellar Medium towards the Double Pulsar and the Gum Nebula using Low-Frequency Pulse Broadening Measurements
articles.summary: Long-term timing of the double pulsar system (PSR J0737-3039A/B) has enabled some of the most stringent constraints on strong-field gravity. Yet, despite the system's high profile, there have been very few observations at frequencies below 300 MHz, where pulse broadening due to interstellar scattering becomes significant. Measurements of the pulse broadening timescale and its frequency scaling, $τ_\mathrm{s}\proptoν^α$ (where $α$ is the scattering spectral index), provide valuable constraints on the structure of the scattering medium. articles.title: Pulse Morphology and Spectral Study of LPT J1634+44 Using GMRT
articles.summary: Long-period radio transients (LPTs) are a recently discovered class of Galactic coherent radio emitters characterized by rotation periods of minutes to hours and highly polarized radio pulses. Their nature remains uncertain, with proposed scenarios invoking isolated or binary systems containing neutron stars (NSs) or white dwarfs (WDs). We investigate the nature of CHIME/ILT J1634+44 through multi-band observations with the Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope (GMRT), examining its pulse morphology, spectral evolution, and timing behavior. articles.title: A 36.34-day Sub-Neptune Candidate Transiting the Nearby K Dwarf TIC 402710280
articles.summary: We report a transiting sub-Neptune candidate with a period of 36.34 days around TIC 402710280 (TYC 9041-03677-1), a K dwarf of TESS magnitude 9.24 at 66.8 pc that the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) has observed only in full-frame images. Four transits, recorded between 2021 and 2026 in Sectors 39, 93, 100 and 102 and reduced by three independent pipelines, share a depth of $2092 \pm 47$ ppm and a duration of $5.27 \pm 0.05$ h. articles.title: Kinematic structure and age of a Scorpius--Centaurus subcomponent: implications for PDS 70 planetary system
articles.summary: PDS~70, the only system with two directly imaged protoplanets embedded in their natal disk, is a benchmark for giant-planet formation theory. Interpreting the planetary luminosities requires a precise age for the host star, but the widely adopted isochronal age of $5.4\pm1.0$~Myr is substantially younger than ages inferred for the Upper Centaurus--Lupus (UCL) population with which it is associated. articles.title: Constraints on the Progenitor of SN 2023bee from its Nebular-Phase Spectra
articles.summary: We present late-time photometry (~100-400 days after peak) and nebular-phase optical/NIR spectroscopy (100-360 days) of the Type Ia supernova (SN Ia) SN 2023bee. This SN Ia was observed TESS immediately before and after explosion and showed a relatively weak early excess light-curve feature detected in multiple UV and optical bands. Possible explanations for this early excess feature include interaction between the SN ejecta and a non-degenerate companion, or the decay of radioactive isotopes synthesized near the ejecta surface in a sub-$\text{M}_\text{Ch}$ double-detonation scenario. articles.title: Hyperonic Direct-Urca Neutrino Emission with Lattice-QCD-Informed Form Factors
articles.summary: We investigate the sensitivity of direct-Urca neutrino emission in hyperonic neutron-star matter to the structure and momentum dependence of baryonic transition form factors. Using the zero-temperature FSU2H relativistic mean-field equation of state, we derive the relativistic emissivity for general spin-$1/2$ baryon transitions with the complete six form-factor contribution. We compare conventional static flavor-SU(3) couplings with vacuum lattice-QCD-informed form factors, using direct lattice vacuum input for $n\rightarrow p$ and $Λ\rightarrow p$ and a hybrid construction for the remaining hyperonic channels. articles.title: Dynamical response of a protoplanetary disk to an FU Ori-type outburst
articles.summary: Episodic accretion events onto young stars can significantly change the global structure of their surrounding protoplanetary disks. Using radiation hydrodynamical simulations with the HURAKAN code, we study the response of the outer passive disk to a powerful FU Ori-type outburst. Disk heating initiates a factor-of-two increase in the vertical scale-height, which develops on a local keplerian timescale. This effectively launches an outward travelling wave with a bump whose radial position changes with time as $r_{b}\sim t^{2/3}$. articles.title: Entering the Era of Circumplanetary Ring Detection with Direct Imaging
articles.summary: Rings are ubiquitous among the giant planets in the Solar System, yet their presence around exoplanets remains observationally unconstrained. As direct imaging missions such as the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope approach first light, understanding the influence of circumplanetary rings on reflected light photometry is critical for the accurate interpretation and follow-up of direct imaging observations. articles.title: Detecting Exoplanetary Rings with Roman CGI Reflected Light Phase Curve Observations
articles.summary: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope's Coronagraph Instrument (CGI) will provide the first opportunity to directly detect mature giant exoplanets in reflected light. However, most known radial-velocity planets lie near CGI's sensitivity limit. In contrast, Saturn-like rings around these planets may be much more accessible: our models show that rings can outshine their host planets by one to two orders of magnitude or more, making them easier to detect than the planets themselves. articles.title: Clustering of JWST LRDs. Implications for PBHs and other early-forming seeds
articles.summary: We use the observed abundance and spatial clustering of JWST little red dots (LRDs) over z = 4--8 to confront two formation scenarios: the standard picture in which LRDs form in virialized dark-matter halos, and one in which they are seeded by a dynamically subdominant population of primordial black holes (PBHs). articles.title: Foreground dependence of the 20 GeV Galactic halo gamma-ray excess and its proposed connection to the LUX-ZEPLIN event
articles.summary: We assess the dark matter interpretation of the 20 GeV gamma-ray halo excess reported by Totani and its proposed connection to the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) high-energy nuclear-recoil event, which independently favors dark matter masses above about 200 GeV. Using fifteen years of Fermi-LAT data, we reproduce the excess under the original assumptions and test it against 281 Galactic diffuse emission configurations, three descriptions of the Fermi bubbles, four of Loop I, and uniform and X-ray-brightness-weighted eROSITA bubbles templates. articles.title: Survey of Orion Disks with ALMA (SODA) IV: Millimeter variability of protoplanetary disks
articles.summary: Context. Short-term millimeter-wavelength variability in Class II young stellar objects (YSOs) has been considered minimal, often dismissed as very rare in ALMA-based studies on short timescales. articles.title: A Hectospec Spectroscopic Census of Kinematic Members in the Orion Nebula Cluster
articles.summary: We present a comprehensive spectroscopic census of the Orion Nebula Cluster (ONC), based primarily on low-resolution optical spectroscopy obtained with MMT/Hectospec. We derive spectral types, youth indicators, and accretion diagnostics for 1513 stars located in the ONC region, enabling the identification and characterization of pre-main-sequence stars. We combine these measurements with a kinematic membership analysis based on Gaia Data Release 3 astrometry to identify and confirm cluster members. articles.title: Andreev Beta Conversion and Bulk Viscosity in Superfluid Neutron-Star Matter
articles.summary: Bulk viscosity in neutron-star matter is attributed to the phase lag between a density oscillation and weak beta equilibration. articles.title: The Atmospheric Chemistry and Surface Interactions on Mars (ACSIOM) Workshop 2025
articles.summary: The ACSIOM workshop was held in Cambridge from 10th-12th November 2025. Its primary aims were twofold: 1) to gather UK researchers involved in Mars atmospheric science to identify current shortcomings and challenges in the field, and 2) to discuss possible collaborations and future steps needed to maximise the research output from current and future Mars missions. Workshop attendees spanned a wide range of subjects and disciplines, from atmospheric modellers and surface scientists to experimental chemists and Earth/Venus/exoplanet scientists. articles.title: ExHaLe-jet: Modeling blazar jets with an extended hadro-leptonic radiation code
articles.summary: Blazars - active galaxies with the jet pointing at Earth - emit across all electromagnetic wavelengths. As the one-zone model becomes increasingly inadequate to describe blazar emission, more elaborate models are needed. In order to self-consistently describe the entire electromagnetic spectrum, extended jet models are necessary. Notably, kinetic descriptions of extended jets can provide the temporal and spatial evolution of the particle species and the full electromagnetic output. articles.title: SN 2025wiu: A Type Ib Supernova with Post-Peak Optical Rebrightening
articles.summary: We present optical photometric and optical/near-infrared spectroscopic observations of SN 2025wiu, a Type Ib supernova (SN) at z = 0.046927. The r-band light curve exhibits an initial maximum of approximately -18.2 mag, followed by a weaker optical rebrightening reaching approximately -17.8 mag at +38 days in the rest frame relative to the first maximum. articles.title: Impact of neutron captures on the r-process: I. Propagation of statistical model uncertainties
articles.summary: Background: The r-process is responsible for producing about half of the elements heavier than iron in the Universe, but the underlying nuclear physics is still largely inaccessible to experiments and relies on theoretical calculations. Purpose: We aim to quantify the impact of statistical model uncertainties on the r-process with a large set of neutron-capture rates within the Hauser-Feshbach framework with varied statistical model parameters. articles.title: Exploring Cosmic Rays from Gravity-Limited Acceleration at Supermassive Black Holes
articles.summary: We show that horizon-scale magnetic fields around supermassive black holes (SMBHs), only limited by gravity, yield a universal, model-independent ceiling on electromagnetic energy density. articles.title: Prospects for Simultaneously Detecting Long and Short Duration Gravitational Waves from Pulsar Glitches with Current and Future Detectors
articles.summary: The internal mechanisms that drive the sudden change in rotation frequency in pulsar glitches could emit gravitational waves (GWs) at multiple time scales. The potential for GW analyses to detect both long and short forms of emission ("tCW-like" and "burst-like") improves as the detectors increase in sensitivity. We aim to examine how future detectors fare in making this joint measurement. articles.title: Three-dimensional spatial modelling of nuclear de-excitation lines
articles.summary: Galactic cosmic rays (GCRs) are thought to originate from shock acceleration in supernova remnants, but interstellar ionization rates suggest an additional low-energy cosmic-ray (LECR) component. LECRs excite nuclei in the ISM, producing MeV gamma-ray line emission through subsequent de-excitation. Observations of this emission can constrain the LECR flux, morphology, and acceleration mechanisms. We construct all-sky maps of Galactic de-excitation emission using three-dimensional (3D) CR distribution models. articles.title: A blazar is a blazar is a blazar ... Comparing long-term varaibility properties of PKS 1510-089 and PKS 2155-304
articles.summary: Blazars are typically divided by spectral appearance; may that be strength of optical emission lines or the frequency of the synchrotron peak. However, this may say nothing about the variability properties of the various types. Here, we study the long-term variability properties with nearly 20 years of multiwavelength data of one flat-spectrum radio quasar, PKS 1510-089, and one high-frequency-peaked BL Lac object, PKS 2155-304. articles.title: LSST and Keck characterization of outer Main Belt comet P/2026 N2
articles.summary: We characterize comet P/2026 N2, whose outer Main Belt orbit has $a=3.07$ au, $e=0.21$, and $i=2.25^\circ$, using optical observations, archival imaging, and dynamical integrations. Observations from the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) at NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory in 2026 June-July and Keck/LRIS imaging on October 7 show active morphology across perihelion over 102 days. articles.title: Singles in Disguise: Kepler's Low-SNR Single-Transiting Systems as Incompletely Detected Multis
articles.summary: NASA's Kepler mission found more systems with one transiting planet (``singles'') than expected from those with several (``multis''). This excess was first taken as evidence for a Kepler dichotomy -- a second population of intrinsically single or highly inclined systems -- but later work argued that selection effects acting on a single population can reproduce it. Singles also show a puzzling excess of low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) detections relative to multis. articles.title: Identifying deformed exoplanets with JWST and Ariel: A target selection metric for phase curve observations
articles.summary: The shape of an exoplanet encodes fundamental information about its internal structure. For close-in giant planets, strong stellar tidal forces induce measurable deformations that can be probed through high-precision photometry. These deformations are quantified by the fluid Love numbers, which characterise a planet's response to external perturbations and are directly linked to its internal density distribution. articles.title: Chemical Demographics of Star-forming Regions
articles.summary: Our understanding of complex organic chemistry during the formation of stars and planets is shaped by a handful of cherry-picked sources with bright molecular emission lines. This observational bias impedes our assessment of how universal chemical complexity is during star formation. articles.title: A New Method for Constraining 3D Exoplanet Atmospheres: Application to WASP-94A b's Panchromatic Spectrum
articles.summary: A growing number of transiting exoplanets exhibit spectroscopic evidence that their leading and trailing limbs differ. Interpreting these observations is now the limiting step. The standard approach of fitting limb-resolved transit depths results in highly anti-correlated transit depths, and treating them as independent measurements can result in strongly biased ($3σ$) retrieved molecular abundances. articles.title: A Sample of Thick-Disk Stars Hosting Hot Jupiters
articles.summary: We present a homogeneous analysis of 268 confirmed and candidate transiting hot-Jupiter host stars with 4800K < Teff < 6200K. We combine high-resolution TRES spectra, Gaia, 2MASS and WISE photometry, and Gaia astrometry to determine these stars' Teff, log g, Rstar, [alpha/Fe] and [Fe/H]. articles.title: ALMA2040: Submillimeter-wave Limb Sounding of Venus and Mars
articles.summary: Venus and Mars are unique laboratories for understanding the evolution and diversity of terrestrial planets. Despite their broadly similar rocky compositions, their atmospheres, climates, and surface environments have evolved into dramatically different states. Understanding the physical and chemical processes responsible for these divergent pathways is essential for interpreting terrestrial exoplanets and their habitability. articles.title: X-ray point sources towards the giant radio lobes of Centaurus A
articles.summary: Centaurus A (NGC 5128) is the nearest radio galaxy (d = 3.8 Mpc), so individual X-ray point sources can be resolved against its giant radio lobes. articles.title: Are $E>B$ regions essential for particle injection in relativistic magnetic reconnection?
articles.summary: During relativistic magnetic reconnection, X-points ($E>B$ regions at vanishing guide field) have been proposed to play an essential role in injecting particles into the nonthermal population. articles.title: Chemistry on solar system scales
articles.summary: The initial chemical composition of planets, primitive bodies in our solar system, and exoplanets is ultimately set by their nascent protoplanetary disks. Yet observing key carbon-, oxygen-, and nitrogen-bearing molecules (as well as rarer but important sulphur- and phosphorus-bearing species) in the inner (exo)planet-forming zone ($\lesssim 10$~au) remains extremely challenging with current facilities. Therefore, to construct a complete picture of the chemistry of planet formation and understand how (exo)planetary composition is set by physical and chemical processes within the protoplanetary disk, a more powerful observing facility, i.e., ALMA2040, is needed. articles.title: Multi-wavelength Polarization as a Probe of Planet Formation
articles.summary: Polarization reveals details of circumstellar disks that are not readily available from total intensity observations. Via multi-wavelength polarimetric observations of disks, we can trace how planets form, how dust grains evolve at the onset of planet formation, and how magnetic fields (B-fields) influence accretion. Since polarized emission from these disks is typically at levels from 0.5% to a few percent of the total emission, very high sensitivities are needed. articles.title: Time-reversible timestepping in many-body planetary systems
articles.summary: Simulating chaotic planetary system evolution requires resolving small time-scales due to close encounters, scattering, collisions, and more. articles.title: Breakdown of hydrodynamic universality in causal first-order viscous neutron star oscillations
articles.summary: Hydrodynamic modeling of viscous neutron stars requires a choice of theory of relativistic hydrodynamics. articles.title: Planetary system architectures in the final stages of planet formation
articles.summary: The processes in the last stages of planet formation determine the final assembly and composition of planets. After the protoplanetary discs dissipate, a system of planets and planetesimals -- analogues of the Asteroid and Kuiper Belts -- remains. Ongoing collisions between these bodies produce second-generation dust and gas that form a debris disc. Resolved images of such belts allow us to trace the dynamical history of these systems, including giant impacts and planet-belt interactions, during the crucial era from 10 to a few 100 Myr of terrestrial planet formation. articles.title: Planet formation on solar system scales
articles.summary: Giant planets are often regarded as primordial protoplanetary "architects". Their formation and interactions with planetesimals and other planets during and after the protoplanetary disc phase are key to setting the blueprint of the planetary systems we observe today. Catching nascent gas giants is our best opportunity to uncover these crucial steps in the planet formation process and shed light on the origins of our own solar system. Over the last decade, ALMA has revolutionised our understanding of planet formation; still, detecting signatures of Jupiter-like planets has remained out of reach. articles.title: Transient PULSE: Code for the Transient Propagation of UltraLight (pseudo)Scalars to Earth
articles.summary: We present Transient PULSE, a software package that numerically implements a previously developed source-to-detector framework for transient ultralight bosonic signals from astrophysical bursts. Predicting these signals relies on connecting the source emission spectrum to its evolution during propagation and the resulting observables at a terrestrial detector. The package discretizes a user supplied energy spectrum into momentum modes, propagates them through a specified matter density profile and constructs the time-frequency energy density distribution at Earth, accounting for dispersion and in-medium screening effects. articles.title: GRB 181201A: Spectropolarimetric Constraints on Prompt Emission and Magnetic Field Structure
articles.summary: Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) have served as testbeds for high-energy astrophysical phenomena since their discovery over 50 years ago. GRB detections reveal diverse properties across events, complicating efforts to constrain their emission mechanisms, magnetic fields, jet structures, and compositions. Spectropolarimetry is a powerful tool utilized to disentangle these properties. INTEGRAL/IBIS has previously detected three polarized GRBs 041219A ($65\pm 26$%), 061122 ($>$33%) and 140206A ($>$28%). We present the time-integrated and time-resolved analyses of the fourth-polarized GRB 181201A. articles.title: Revealing the Spatial Distribution of Dust and Plasma Solitary Waves in Jupiter's Innermost Magnetosphere Using Juno Waves Observations
articles.summary: Jupiter's faint ring system contains micron- and submicron-sized dust whose dynamics are influenced by the planet's rapidly rotating magnetic field. Optical observations have established the morphology of the main ring and halo, but tenuous dust close to Jupiter remains difficult to characterize. We analyze nearly a decade of in-situ Juno Waves electric-field measurements using a two-stage convolutional neural network to identify and classify dust impacts, solitary waves, and other plasma waves. These in-situ dust-impact detections reveal a radially evolving structure extending well inside the traditionally observed halo. articles.title: Can bosenovae deplete the galactic dark matter?
articles.summary: No: neither through the bosenovae of gravitational atoms formed around stars and compact objects, nor through those of boson stars formed in the galactic dark-matter halo. We assume that all the dark matter consists of ultralight bosons with attractive self-interactions, which can be captured in the gravitational potential of astrophysical objects or condense into self-gravitating configurations. When these systems collapse in a bosenova, part of their mass is turned into relativistic radiation that escapes the galaxy. articles.title: A Parsec-Scale Transient High-Frequency-Peaked Radio Source in the Very Large Array Sky Survey Brightening and Fading over a Decadal Timescale
articles.summary: A subset of active galactic nuclei (AGN) manifests as compact radio sources with peaked radio spectra, commonly referred to as peaked-spectrum (PS) sources. Generally, PS sources are interpreted as young radio jets, but the early evolution of the jet is rarely observed and not fully understood. articles.title: LHAASO Constraints on New-Source Cosmic Rays:Abundance Scenarios and Injection Spectral Indices
articles.summary: Recent LHAASO observations indicate that microquasars and massive star clusters contribute to Galactic cosmic rays, and likely also to the pre-knee spectral hardening. Their markedly different astrophysical environments, compared with supernova remnants (SNRs), may imprint distinct cosmic-ray abundances. We investigate the spectra and composition of new-source cosmic rays under two abundance scenarios: Case-1, the SNR-like composition with enhanced heavy nuclei, and Case-2, the surface abundances of microquasar companion stars. articles.title: The contact frontier in Galactic civilization networks: radial structure and the Galactic habitable zone
articles.summary: The probability of interstellar contact depends not only on the abundance of technological civilizations but also on their spatial connectivity. Treating civilizations as nodes linked whenever their separation is smaller than the distance a signal travels within a communicative lifetime, we determine the radial structure of Galactic civilization networks. An exponential stellar disc replaces the uniform disc of earlier work, and the fraction of stars hosting civilizations may vary with radius as a Galactic Habitable Zone (GHZ). articles.title: Rotochemical heating of neutron stars in 2D
articles.summary: The matter inside a spinning-down neutron star (NS) undergoes a slow compression that may drive it out of chemical equilibrium and, consequently, trigger non-equilibrium nuclear reactions that can heat up the star. This phenomenon is called rotochemical heating, and it is relatively well-investigated in the literature. Historically, it has been studied almost exclusively via 1D spherically symmetric models. However, rapidly rotating NSs are not spherically symmetric. We present pioneering simulations of rotochemical heating in full General Relativity in 2D axially symmetric models without relying on the slow rotation approximation. articles.title: Probing Planet Formation within 10 au: Dust Substructures in Extremely Compact Protoplanetary Disks
articles.summary: ALMA high-resolution surveys have so far focused mainly on large, bright protoplanetary disks, where substructures are routinely detected, leaving compact disks poorly characterized. Yet, the survival of millimeter emission in Class II sources implies that radial drift must have been halted by pressure traps, previously undetected due to limited angular resolution. We present ALMA Band 7 (0.9 mm) continuum observations of 11 of the smallest ($R_{68} < 10$ au) Class II disks in Lupus, reaching $0.02''$ (2 au) resolution, the highest currently available with ALMA at this wavelength. articles.title: Biases in Ringdown Tests of General Relativity from Gravitational-Wave Microlensing
articles.summary: Gravitational-wave (GW) ringdown signals provide a powerful probe of the strong-field regime of general relativity (GR) through black hole spectroscopy and tests of the Kerr hypothesis. However, unmodeled propagation effects can bias the inference of remnant properties and the interpretation of ringdown features. We investigate the impact of gravitational lensing on ringdown inference and tests of GR using GW150914-like simulated signals spanning the long-wavelength, wave-optics, and geometric-optics regimes. articles.title: Revisiting the Optical F-corona from the Artemis II Total Solar Eclipse with RAW Data: How Far Can Consumer JPEG Images Be Trusted for Astronomical Photometry?
articles.summary: We reanalyze the total solar eclipse images taken with a consumer camera during the Artemis II lunar flyby, using the RAW data as ground truth for our previous analysis of the released JPEG image. articles.title: Search for High-Energy Neutrinos from Infrared Flares
articles.summary: IceCube has detected a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos. While its astrophysical origin is unknown, a significant neutrino emission has been observed from the gamma-ray blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Seyfert galaxy NGC 1068. This suggests accretion by supermassive black holes as one of the candidate mechanisms of the diffuse neutrino flux. Indeed, external studies that made use of IceCube data identified candidate sources, including AT2019dsg, likely a stellar tidal disruption event (TDE), and AT2019fdr, associated with an active galactic nucleus (AGN). articles.title: Optical constraints on intranight variability in TeV HBLs from a two-year Asiago Schmidt monitoring campaign
articles.summary: We present a two-year homogeneous optical monitoring campaign of three TeV-emitting high-synchrotron-peaked BL Lac objects, 1ES 1959+650, H 1426+428, and PG 1553+113, carried out with the Asiago Schmidt 67/92 cm telescope. TeV blazars are key targets in high-energy astrophysics, relevant for relativistic jet physics, particle acceleration, multiwavelength variability studies, and, in selected cases, multimessenger programmes. In this context, dense optical monitoring provides a low-energy synchrotron tracer of jet activity over temporal baselines that are difficult to cover continuously with high-energy facilities. articles.title: HD 152384: A 5 Myr old debris disk system showing a gaseous ring of refractory elements at the dust sublimation radius
articles.summary: Context: Circumstellar gas around young stars provides key insights into planet formation and disk evolution.
